newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican ruling party senator defects to opposition.
newsitem.headline: Mexican ruling party senator defects to opposition.

text.p: Ruling party senator Layda Sansores Sanroman defected to the leftist opposition on Tuesday and accepted an invitation to run against her former party for governor of the oil-rich state of Campeche.
Sansores said she had accepted the invitation from the Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD) to seek the state governorship in elections in July next year.
PRD leader Andres Lopez Obrador predicted that the PRD, Mexico's third biggest party, would win its first-ever state governorship with Sansores as its candidate.
The PRD was created in 1988 by a group of disgruntled former members of the long-ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party, which has been in power since 1929.
The PRD has lost much of its strength in recent years but is undergoing a resurgence under the leadership of Lopez, who was elected as party president in July.
